g.title: nc612fb731050
g.text: “True randomness” becomes a regulatory threshold called “acceptable randomness.”

g.title: nf840664a5a6b
g.text: A fair game requires a second operation after randomness: random numbers must be mapped into outcomes.

g.title: n53bc0f02633b
g.text: The RNG seed and the game’s return-to-player percentage belong to different mechanisms.

g.title: na7f72f623ae1
g.text: An online casino decomposes into components that each transform a different kind of state.

g.title: na161989e942c
g.text: A new interface channel can change while the game engine remains the same.

g.title: n4603f822a6de
g.text: Simulation testing does not test “the game” at once; it tests whether one statistical consequence falls inside an acceptable range.

g.title: n7e3ffdaeb239
g.text: Kaneva treated 2D and 3D as alternate interfaces onto one social world rather than as separate destinations.

g.title: na6976645f680
g.text: Kaneva did not merely embed YouTube; it converted a web media object into an object located inside a room.

g.title: nb72aaf1ea7de
g.text: Kaneva's world was designed around ingress: the world remained alive by admitting things that were not produced inside it.

g.title: ndc1c1979865b
g.text: In Kaneva, the virtual house begins to look less like simulated shelter than a spatial operating system for media and identity.

g.title: ne526698c9269
g.text: Kaneva suggests that “entering the world” and “accessing the world” are different operations.

g.title: na0db2ca76b69
g.text: Mozilla Hubs made the URL itself into a door to a 3D world.

g.title: n332965012a20
g.text: In Hubs, pasting a URL could manufacture a manipulable object.

g.title: n0d2b46c01d2b
g.text: Mozilla could close Hubs without making the Hubs code cease to exist.

g.title: naaedca6e18d6
g.text: The metaverse may be representation-independent: 2D and 3D can be clients of the same world.

g.title: nab83e6ea4bd2
g.text: Roblox compiles jurisdiction, age, and platform policy into runtime variables.

g.title: nfb9502ed5b36
g.text: Roblox does not regulate “randomness” uniformly: paid randomness can be conditional while advertising rewards must be predetermined.

g.title: na81340adb7e4
g.text: Minecraft protects the boundary of a server by forbidding its virtual currency from crossing it.

g.title: n86a68d4758a0
g.text: For UK gambling law, the border between game and world can determine whether a loot box counts as gambling.

g.title: n0e59e0f8624a
g.text: The central loot-box evidence problem may be that the platform possesses the experiment while researchers possess only observations.

g.title: nb47b7c8685e1
g.text: Xsolla's Web Shop lets the purchase leave the game while the purchased object stays inside it.

g.title: n6297dadbd3ef
g.text: Xsolla Metasites translates the hyperlink graph into a portal graph.

g.title: neda4febbbc37
g.text: The hidden boundary of Roblox becomes visible on the credit-card statement: “Xsolla*Roblox.”

g.title: nff47f87b57fe
g.text: A Minecraft server can acquire a second body on the web: server in 3D, commercial identity in 2D.

g.title: n36f37fc1527b
g.text: The casino is not the building: gambling is a topology of value, chance, and payout that can wear any architecture.

g.title: n6350552500e6
g.text: Second Life turns legal jurisdiction into literal geography: some avatars are not permitted to enter the region.

g.title: n848fb5d31a47
g.text: A worthless virtual object can legalize a chance mechanic by failing to become money.

g.title: n21ce33704ab0
g.text: Roblox's marble fountain turns a randomized transaction into a tiny piece of world physics.

g.title: n72e54b281226
g.text: Roblox's value membrane is asymmetric: player money can enter a random-item economy while creator earnings can leave as dollars.

g.title: n74b0b836c24e
g.text: Xsolla turns gambling-adjacentness into catalog metadata: “Mark as paid randomized reward.”

g.title: nb375a5247af1
g.text: The treasure chest disappears completely in Xsolla's API: “open loot box” is a remote state mutation with three identifiers.

g.title: ne2c5c5d933cd
g.text: Minecraft bans “gambling” as an all-ages world-content failure while separately engineering currencies so they cannot escape the server.

g.title: n90dfa62ef288
g.text: The boundary of the virtual world is part of the gambling machine.

g.title: n1295960fb9fd
g.text: A program can be a choreography of state transformations

g.title: nccf0b00492e0
g.text: A world can exceed its rendering

g.title: nc9838cf7a5d2
g.text: A world is partly defined by what cannot cross its border

g.title: nd20cb8677ee1
g.text: Do not mistake a component for the system

g.title: n09183d220c88
g.text: Economic operations can masquerade as world physics

g.title: n3fcace6ffaf4
g.text: Information becomes matter by acquiring verbs

g.title: n530da92205ad
g.text: Mechanics acquire meaning from transaction topology

g.title: n8dda9d237a34
g.text: Some world walls are safety mechanisms

g.title: n807fb1fc1788
g.text: Tests construct what can be known about programs

g.title: n046a88ebecb7
g.text: The box is an interface fiction over a state transition

g.title: nf51f363c00f4
g.text: The membrane changes the meaning of the mechanism

g.title: nf4179a96d53e
g.text: The world can camouflage the transaction

g.title: n8a25678ae270
g.text: The world has a commercial exoskeleton

g.title: nce29e4587fa5
g.text: The world is invariant; the interface conjugates it

g.title: n2b1cc2a4418b
g.text: The world is not its rendering

g.title: n8a7dcee61c48
g.text: The world is not the picture of the world

g.title: n890eb4fff92a
g.text: What travels when software crosses media?

g.title: n9d839c74ffa0
g.text: Who gets to observe the world?

g.title: nd90e224bbb1d
g.text: Interfaces can change without changing semantics

g.title: n64870d9cbd9e
g.text: Passing is indexed to a test

g.title: nc1ae5a89585a
g.text: The map between number and event

g.title: n7bc1288dc7da
g.text: What dies when a world closes?
